science.basis: Independent affected prose and neighboring equation judgment only.

checks.conclusion: F1 still combines the spring force and wire weight only. The film pull is explicitly separate, and equilibrium does not remove the individual pulls.
One-face F, equal interface conditions and a common upward direction are introduced before -2F. The two-factor is expressly conditional; a single interface contributes only its own pull.

Near-equilibrium slow motion, negligible friction/viscous loss, stable interfaces and approximately constant force remain explicit. Combined downward-force work is positive, upward film-force work is negative, and gravity's contribution is not counted twice.

The ideal reversible fixed-temperature model is explained locally. Surface-work increase is identified with the surface free-energy measure, while possible heat exchange and the distinction from the whole system's internal-energy change remain explicit. The textbook/model surface-energy notation is retained.

S1/S2 are explicitly the before/after areas of the same one face. The unchanged adjacent equation uses S2-S1=lh. U_{surface1}/U_{surface2}, A=2 sigma lh and the full registered area erratum are unchanged.

Stable temperature, composition and surrounding medium constrain the approximately constant sigma model. The uniform flat contact condition is retained. The equality of the two work expressions and cancellation of the common nonzero 2h factor for positive extension are now explained without altering F=sigma l.

The tiny-patch gloss preserves the local tangent-plane direction and perpendicularity to the local boundary. Different boundary-segment directions must still be considered when summing forces, and the contact length is not the frame perimeter.

Force in newtons is distinguished from sigma in newtons per meter. Joules are named as energy units. J/m^2=N m/m^2=N/m remains unchanged and retains the surface-energy interpretation under the stated model.
